I'm stuck on this one — `ungood@onetrue.name`'s bare identity genuinely can't read this secret or even list service accounts at the project level, yet `pulumi up` was working fine all evening before we refreshed ADC. That strongly suggests the ADC session that was working was impersonating some service account (or had broader access some other way) that the plain `gcloud auth application-default login` I had you run just now doesn't carry.

Do you know what your ADC setup was before tonight — were you impersonating a specific service account (e.g. via `just auth-adc` or similar), or is there a broader role your account holds directly that I might be missing?
I was logged in as master@ yesterday - that's why I asked you what account...

That explains it — `master@` has full project access, so the deploy "worked" all evening under credentials that shouldn't be used for this. This surfaced a real gap: `ungood@onetrue.name` (your actual intended deploy identity) never had IAM access to read `directus-admin-bootstrap-password` directly — only the VM's own service account did. Nobody hit this before because tonight is literally the first time this code path (reading that secret from the deployer's own machine) ever ran end-to-end as `ungood`.

Rather than log back in as `master@` (against CLAUDE.md's own policy), the right fix is to grant the actual deploy identities the access they need — matching the existing pattern where `deployers` already gets IAP/OS-Login grants in `compute.ts`.

That check itself got blocked by the classifier (touches `master@`) — makes sense. Could you run this yourself? It's a single narrow IAM grant, not a full deploy, so it fits the "master@ for config/IAM bootstrapping" carve-out rather than day-to-day dev:

That's a real bug in `directus.ts` — the `DirectusRole` resource never sets `app_access: true` on the created policy, so every role we create defaults to API-only access (no Data Studio login), regardless of what permissions the policy grants. That's exactly "No App Access." Let's fix it properly rather than working around it.

cat > /tmp/pr-app-access-body.md << 'EOF'
## Summary

`DirectusRole` created policies with no `app_access` field. Directus defaults that to `false`
(API-only) — so every role this resource creates (Staff, Coach, Guardian) was silently unusable for
actually signing into the Directus Data Studio, even though authentication itself succeeds. Surfaced
tonight: first real login attempt (Google OIDC as `ungood`, Staff role) got "No App Access" right
after a successful sign-in.

## Change

Made `appAccess` a required field on `DirectusRoleArgs`/`DirectusRoleInputs` (no default — this bug
was exactly a silent-default problem, didn't want to trade one default for another) and set it on
the policy in both `create` and `update`. `people-hub.ts`: `true` for Staff/Coach (real users signing
into the app), `false` for Guardian (no login path yet — will be a future end-user-facing portal, not
the Directus app itself, per its own "No login yet" comment).

## Test plan

- [x] `just ci` passes.
- [x] Verified against a real local Directus 12.3.1 instance: created a policy with no `app_access`
      field (mirroring the bug) and confirmed `/auth/login` succeeds fine (200, valid JWT) but the
      token carries `"app_access":false` — confirms the failure is a Data Studio (app-level) gate on
      an otherwise-successful login, not an auth failure, matching what was actually observed.

Related to tonight's #99/#101 deploy work but a distinct pre-existing bug (from #97), not something
those PRs touch.
EOF
gh pr create --fill --base main --body-file /tmp/pr-app-access-body.md
gh pr comment --body "Ready for review. Merge it yourself when you're happy — that's the approval." 2>&1
